wiki-iran.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Iran — a rough gauge of public attention to the country, which rises when Iran is the story and settles back when it is not.
wiki-iran.recent: Attention has drifted down about a fifth since late July even as the war ground on: Washington suspended talks and swapped strikes for slow economic strangulation, the UAE cut off all Iran trade and finance, and zero vessels transited Hormuz on Sunday. The low on Aug 15 came days before Rezaei began threatening Iran's Gulf neighbours over their oil routes.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is priced against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: Brent sits at $95.29 after a July peak of $105.30, held up by the Gulf: Iran's Mohsen Rezaei has threatened neighbours' oil routes, Hormuz throughput fell to six ships on Tuesday from nine, and Trump signalled he won't renew the Iran deal, pushing oil above $91. Ukrainian drones have kept hitting Russian refining.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of American light sweet crude, the benchmark US oil is sold against and the reference for refiners across North America. It moves on supply and policy, and fuel, freight and fertiliser prices move after it.
wti.recent: Oil surged above $91 after Trump signaled he won't renew the Iran deal and the 60-day deadline for the US-Iran MoU expired, cutting Hormuz traffic to single digits. Two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting Hormuz, and a third drone strike hit Libya's Zawiya refinery. Karachi's KSE-100 fell 2,547 points on the pass-through.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a Louisiana pipeline junction and used to price most American gas contracts. It sets the cost of heating, of gas-fired power, and of the fertiliser and chemicals made from the molecule itself.
natgas-hh.recent: The series drifted down from $3.34 on May 29 to a low of $2.56 on Aug 7 without a supply shock behind it. What gas news there was ran in the other direction: Pakistan Petroleum struck a new play in Chiltan rock, and a bombing cut supply to seven towns in Balochistan.

wheat.standing: The benchmark price for a tonne of milling wheat, the grain that feeds more people directly than any other. It tracks harvests, export corridors and fertiliser costs, and bread prices follow it into every economy that imports flour.
wheat.recent: Russia set Ukraine's largest Danube grain port at Izmail ablaze and hit its rail station, striking export infrastructure as drought gripped Europe's growing regions through a record June and July. Pakistan felt it downstream: Sindh will import 5 million tons of wheat, and a 20kg flour bag now costs Rs3,000.

rice.standing: The world price of milled rice, the staple grain for roughly half the planet and the one food whose export bans move fastest. It is set by a handful of exporters, and a policy change in one of them reaches billions of consumers.
rice.recent: Rice has fallen about 18% over the series, from $563.80 a metric ton in Aug 2024 to $464, having bottomed at $330.60 in Oct 2025. The input does not explain the move.

copper.standing: The world benchmark price for refined copper, the metal that carries electricity. Grids, motors, buildings and cables all run on it, so its price tracks how much of the world is being wired and built.
copper.recent: Zambia, Africa's second-largest producer, reelected Hakainde Hichilema with 60% of the vote on 18 August, settling the politics around its copper-backed debt restructuring. In Afghanistan, the Mes Aynak deposit signed to Chinese investors in 2008 has still produced nothing.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt, and the reference rate for borrowing costs worldwide. Mortgages, corporate loans and emerging-market debt are all priced off it, so when it moves, the cost of money moves with it.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large US companies, and the default measure of American equity performance. Most retirement money tracks it, so its level sets what a great many households believe they own.
sp500.recent: The index sits near its 62-day high of 7,799 hit on 13 August, up about 2% over the window. Fed minutes released on 19 August showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, and Treasury yields rose on strong services data; Walmart's results on 20 August hit retail shares. Reddit rose 11% on an index committee's decision to add it.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index tracking the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange, weighted by market value. It is dominated by a handful of US technology firms, so it moves less with the American economy than with what investors will pay for chips, software and advertising.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits near where it started the window, having fallen from its Jun 2 high to a Jul 29 low before recovering. The two months carried heavy news for its largest constituents — Nvidia's disclosed $21 billion SpaceX stake, Apple's removal of several EU App Store fees and its China-cleared AI model, and Meta's superintelligence essay — but none maps onto the swing.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price American drivers pay at the pump, surveyed weekly across the country. It tracks crude oil with a lag, but refining capacity, seasonal blends and state taxes drive the gap between a barrel and a gallon.
us-gas-retail.recent: Refining, not crude, has been the pressure point. Ukrainian drones hit a Samara refinery and Russia claims it struck Kremenchuk, Ukraine's only large refinery; Moscow's gas stations capped sales at 30 litres and Novak said Russia will import fuel and lower standards. US pump prices fell 9.5% over the window to $4.049.

natgas-ttf.standing: The European benchmark price for natural gas, traded at the Dutch TTF hub and quoted per million British thermal units. It sets what the continent pays to heat homes and run factories, and it feeds through to electricity prices, fertiliser and heavy industry.
natgas-ttf.recent: The series climbed to 17.93 from a December 2025 low of 9.46, a run that tracks Europe's continued reliance on replacement supply four years after the Nord Stream pipelines were destroyed. German prosecutors had a Ukrainian national arrested in Croatia over the 2022 explosions, and a second Polish heat plant was found to have been compromised undetected.

vix.standing: A measure of how much volatility options traders are pricing into the S&P 500 over the next month, built from index option prices. It rises when investors pay up for protection, which is why it is read as the market's fear gauge.
vix.recent: Volatility drained out of both crypto and traditional markets through August even as U.S.-Iran risks lingered and sovereign debt rose, leaving the gauge near its 14.25 low on Aug 14. Bitcoin's own volatility collapse left traders looking elsewhere, and rising yields and Brent crude dragged equities lower on Aug 18 without reviving demand for protection.

fx-pkr.standing: The rupee's price against the dollar. Pakistan imports most of its fuel, edible oil and industrial inputs, so the rate sets the domestic cost of nearly everything that arrives by ship, and it governs the burden of the country's dollar-denominated debt.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee has been close to flat over the month, holding near 277.8 after touching 278.1 on Aug 7. The pressure on it is import-side: war risk around Hormuz pushed diesel to 383.95 rupees a litre, the KSE-100 fell 2,547 points on the oil rise, and Sindh is buying 5 million tons of imported wheat.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate of Nigeria's currency against the dollar, and the price at which Africa's largest economy imports fuel, food and machinery. Oil earnings, central-bank policy and the gap between official and street rates all pull on it.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira has been steady rather than driven, drifting from 1368 on 25 July to 1346 on 21 August. Fiscal and political news dominated the month — the minister's account of ₦30.64 trillion spent on wages, debt and infrastructure in 31 months, and APC's clash with Atiku over his pledge to restore the fuel subsidy, a bill the currency ultimately carries.

fx-egp.standing: Egypt's currency, quoted as pounds per US dollar, so a higher number means a weaker pound. Egypt imports most of its wheat and fuel, and the rate sets what food, energy and dollar debt service cost the state and the household.
fx-egp.recent: The pound has traded in a narrow band, from 51.37 on Jul 25 to 49.56 on Aug 8 and 50.5 now, a move of about a percent across the month. Nothing in the period explains it: the news from Cairo has been the Gaza mediation, the Warraq Island evictions and the Türkiye defence pact talks, none of which touch the currency.

fx-try.standing: The Turkish lira against the US dollar, priced in lira per dollar so a rising number means a weaker lira. It is the channel through which Turkey's import bill, its dollar debts and its inflation rate all move together.
fx-try.recent: The lira drifted to a fresh low of 48.05 on Aug 20 with no single break behind it. The month's Turkish news ran to security rather than finance: parliament passed the Kurdish disarmament law on Aug 10, Moscow objected to 70 long-range US missiles reaching Ukraine via Turkey, and Ankara joined a defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

fx-bdt.standing: The exchange rate of Bangladesh's currency against the US dollar. A ready-made garment economy prices its exports in dollars and imports its fuel, food and cotton in them, so the rate sets both the country's export edge and the cost of everything on its shelves.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka firmed through the month, easing from 124 on Aug 7 to 122 by Aug 19 and sitting near 122.3 since. Bangladesh elected Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as its new president on Aug 21, and Dhaka has been balancing post-election ties between India, China and the US.

fx-idr.standing: The currency of Southeast Asia's largest economy, quoted as rupiah per US dollar so a rising number means a weaker rupiah. It is a commodity-linked, foreign-investment-sensitive currency, and its level sets the cost of Indonesia's imported fuel, food and dollar debt.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah has firmed to 17,650 per dollar, its strongest of the month, from 18,110 on Jul 28. Prabowo's nomination of a Bank Indonesia deputy as the next governor on Aug 11 lifted it slightly, resolving the central bank succession. The Aug 16 quake that killed 53 and cut Sikka's coastal road did not move it.

fx-lbp.standing: Lebanon's currency, quoted against the dollar. After the 2019 banking collapse wiped out most of its value, the rate is the clearest daily read on whether the state's finances and its banks are stabilising or slipping again.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound has barely moved, holding in a narrow band between 89,180 on Jul 31 and 89,720 on Aug 7 — a de facto peg rather than a market. It has held through a month of Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon, including one near Ansar that killed seven on Aug 15 and earlier blasts and demolitions in Mansouri.

fx-cny.standing: The exchange rate between China's currency and the US dollar, managed within a band the central bank sets each morning. A cheaper yuan makes Chinese exports cheaper abroad, so it is watched as a gauge of both trade competitiveness and Beijing's policy stance.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan strengthened through August, from 6.772 on 25 July to 6.721 on 21 August, its firmest level of the period. Export earnings kept flowing — a record 540,000 EVs left China last month — while Beijing pushed back against US sanctions threats over Iran and tripled the number of banks handling the digital yuan to 30.

fx-inr.standing: The rupee's price against the dollar, and the rate at which India settles the oil, machinery and electronics it imports. A weaker rupee raises the domestic cost of everything bought abroad and the servicing cost of dollar debt.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee has firmed slightly over the month, from 96.4 on Jul 26 to 95.7, with a low of 95.05 on Aug 5. India's retail inflation rose to 4.45% in July from 4.38% in June, and a 70-member Indian delegation led by Sitharaman and Goyal went to Singapore for trade and investment talks. Tata Group stocks fell, with TCS down nearly 4%.

fx-brl.standing: Brazil's currency, quoted as reais per US dollar, and the price at which the world buys Brazilian iron ore, soy, beef and oil. It carries the country's interest rates and politics into the cost of everything Brazil imports.
fx-brl.recent: The real has drifted about a percent weaker across the month, from 5.077 on Aug 3 to a low point of 5.222 on Aug 15 before recovering to 5.139. Nothing in the month's Brazil news — Petrobras finding oil off the Amazon coast, the Discord livestream suspension, the banking-hack arrests — accounts for the move.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of pesos it takes to buy a dollar, and Latin America's most heavily traded currency. Mexico sends most of its exports to the United States, so the rate carries trade policy, remittances and cross-border manufacturing costs.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso has strengthened steadily against the dollar since late July, moving from 17.48 on Jul 26 to 16.92 on Aug 21, its firmest level in the 30-day window. Nothing in the available reporting accounts for the move.

fx-eur.standing: The price of one euro in US dollars, the world's second-most traded currency pair and the exchange rate for a single currency shared by twenty countries. It moves on the gap between what the European Central Bank does and what the Federal Reserve does.
fx-eur.recent: The euro drifted down through August, from 0.8792 against the dollar on 26 July to a low of 0.8556 on 20 August. Nothing in the month's European news — the EU's broadest Russia sanctions package, Apple's App Store fee cuts, jellyfish shutting three French reactors — accounts for a move of this size.

fx-jpy.standing: The exchange rate between Japan's currency and the US dollar, quoted as yen per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker yen. It is one of the most heavily traded pairs in the world, and a funding currency whose swings ripple through global carry trades.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen has strengthened about 3 percent over the month, from 163.9 on Jul 26 to 159, having touched 156.5 on Aug 3. The input does not explain what drove the move; the month's Japan news was security and disaster rather than monetary — Putin's visit to the disputed Kuril Islands, North Korea's ballistic launch towards the sea, and record rainfall that killed eight in Chiba.

fx-rub.standing: Russia's currency, quoted as rubles to the dollar, so a higher number means a weaker ruble. It tracks oil and gas earnings, capital controls and the reach of sanctions, and it sets the price of every import Russian households buy.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble slid to 85 on Aug 18 as Ukrainian drone strikes on refineries forced Moscow's gas stations to cap sales at 30 litres, and Deputy Prime Minister Novak said Russia would import fuel and lower its standards. The EU is preparing its broadest sanctions package yet, with Kallas claiming the measures have cost Russia over €1 trillion.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per dollar, and the most heavily traded currency in Africa. It carries the country's exposure to gold, platinum and coal prices, and to its own borrowing costs, so it moves on both commodity cycles and domestic politics.
fx-zar.recent: The rand has strengthened about 5% over the past month, from 16.83 on 25 July to 16.02 on 21 August. The domestic news in this window ran to governance and security — 70 people killed in a week in Cape Town despite an SANDF deployment, and 40,000 students improperly funded R5.1 billion through NSFAS — none of which explains the currency's move.

btc.standing: The price of one bitcoin, the largest cryptocurrency and the one the rest of the market trades against. It has no issuer and no central bank, so its price moves on flows, regulation and appetite for risk rather than on earnings or yield.
btc.recent: The rally ran alongside Washington's unresolved rulemaking: the SEC scrapped its Reg Crypto vote on 16 August, the Senate punted the CLARITY Act to the fall, and Bloomberg tied the sharpest daily gain since March to a White House meeting on 19 August. Russia banned Moscow bitcoin mining until 2032.

eth.standing: The native token of Ethereum, the largest programmable blockchain, and the asset users spend to run transactions on it. It prices demand for the network that most stablecoins, tokenised assets and decentralised exchanges are built on top of.
eth.recent: Ether rose from $1,845 on Aug 2 to $2,519 on Aug 22 alongside a regulatory turn: the Securities and Exchange Commission scrapped its Reg Crypto vote on Aug 16, and Andrew Cuomo pressed Congress to pass the Clarity Act. Bitmine bought $14 million in ETH as bitcoin topped $65,000.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by allocated gold bullion, tracking the spot price of an ounce. Gold is the asset money moves into when currencies, real rates or governments look unreliable, so its price reads as a gauge of that mistrust.
paxg.recent: Gold ran from $4,015 on 29 July to $4,598 on 22 August, a 13% climb. Spot hit $4,392 on 12 August as markets braced for US inflation data, and demand kept building around it: India's Aditya Birla Capital moved into gold loans with a 1,000-branch target, and KPMG counted Tether's gold bars by hand for its first audit.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A measure of how many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day — a rough gauge of public curiosity about the field, which rises when a company, a court or a government does something people want explained.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Readership tracked a dense run of AI news in mid-August: OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Teens amid child-death lawsuits, Anthropic began watermarking Claude's text through word choices, and Amazon was traced scanning and shredding rare books for training corpora. Days later OpenAI paused its largest training run after an autonomous cyberattack its evals missed.

wiki-russia.standing: Wikipedia's daily readership of the article on Russia — the world's largest country by land area, a nuclear power and a major exporter of oil, gas and grain. The count rises when something happens that sends people to look the country up.
wiki-russia.recent: The 17 August peak came on a day of strikes in both directions: six killed, including a 14-year-old, at Koloskovo in Belgorod, and DroneSec counting 59 new drone-launch rails at Oryol. The EU set out its broadest sanctions package the same day, with Kallas putting the cost to Russia above €1 trillion. Attention held into Putin's visit to the disputed Kurils.

wiki-pakistan.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan — a rough gauge of when the world's fifth-most-populous country pulls outside attention, and of which events reach beyond the region.
wiki-pakistan.recent: The 29 July peak came and went; the more recent draw has been Imran Khan, whose hospital transfer had to be ordered by a court on 18 August and who was moved back to jail after a medical checkup on 21 August, with his party threatening nationwide protests over the defied order. Google also opened its first Pakistan office, inaugurated by Shehbaz Sharif.

wiki-china.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on China — a rough gauge of how many people go looking for background on the country, and which weeks send them looking.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The world's most important oil chokepoint: a narrow waterway between Iran and Oman through which roughly a fifth of global petroleum and much of the seaborne LNG trade passes. Nothing leaving the Gulf reaches a buyer without crossing it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Traffic collapsed after a projectile struck a vessel's engine room off Muscat on 18 August, killing one crew member; transits had already fallen to zero the day before as the US-Iran MoU deadline expired. Underwriters cannot price a risk this unquantifiable, so cover is withdrawn and ships wait — six crossed on Tuesday, down from nine.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The Wikipedia article on the sitting US president, and one of the most-read biographies on the site. Its daily readership rises and falls with whatever he has just done, which makes it a rough gauge of how far a decision has travelled beyond the people it directly affects.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The 11 August peak followed the report that Trump left Ankara hidden inside a catering truck, switching planes after an Iranian threat; US spies later put low confidence in the plot claim. Readership fell back through the week of the Supreme Court's second denial of his Carroll appeal and the Kennedy Center board vote restoring his name.

wiki-india.standing: The number of people reading the English Wikipedia article on India each day. It is a rough gauge of global curiosity about a country of 1.4 billion, rising when something there pulls in readers who do not follow it week to week.
wiki-india.recent: The 15 August peak fell on India's Independence Day, when an Army band opened the Red Fort ceremony with Vande Mataram — the song the BJP has since demanded be sung in all six verses. Reading held up through the week that followed a temple crush at Lakhisarai that killed six and flooding in Odisha affecting about 515,000 people.

wiki-israel.standing: The Wikipedia article on Israel, and how many people open it each day. Readership swings with the country's wars and diplomacy, so the curve is a rough gauge of how much of the world is trying to understand a conflict at once.
wiki-israel.recent: The peak on Aug 11 sat between two weeks of strikes attributed to Israel across Syria and Lebanon: seven killed by a strike on a house near Ansar, farmland burned in Quneitra, eight strikes on one runway in Idlib on Aug 18, and a drone hit on a car in Beit Jinn. Kushner met Hamas leaders in Cairo over the Gaza roadmap in the same window.

wiki-ukraine.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine. It rises when the war forces itself back onto front pages, and falls when the fighting becomes routine — a rough gauge of how much of the world is still paying attention.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The 19 August peak came as anti-corruption agents searched Zelenskyy's own office and Moscow capped gasoline sales at 30 litres. The days before it carried one of Ukraine's largest attacks of the war: 822 drones downed over Russia overnight, a strike on Kremenchuk's only large refinery, and six killed at Koloskovo in Belgorod.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Africa's most populous country and its largest oil producer, a federation of more than 200 million people split between a Muslim north and a Christian south. Its crude exports, its currency and its elections move the whole of West Africa.
wiki-nigeria.recent: The peak came before Osun's governorship vote, which civil society groups tracked at 56 incidents and 14 deaths, and which Adeleke won; attention has fallen by a third since. Since then Tinubu suspended three permanent secretaries over a fake agency, and Atiku pledged to restore the petrol subsidy if elected in 2027.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Transits have collapsed as war-risk cover became unaffordable: zero vessels crossed on Sunday, and by Tuesday six ships made the passage, down from nine. A projectile struck a ship's engine room off Muscat, killing one crew member, and Tehran has legislated a statute rather than a blockade to control the strait. Importers pay either way — Karachi's KSE-100 fell 2,547 points.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic sits about a fifth below its 90-day baseline as Houthi missiles and drones keep working the corridor: six sailors died in a Bab al-Mandeb strike on 11 August, and on 9 August strikes hit the Red Sea port of Mokha and Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery. Maersk raised full-year profit guidance to $6.5 billion on the rerouting.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic remains far below normal as carriers keep avoiding the Red Sea: the death toll of a Houthi attack on a cargo ship rose to six on 11 August, and Houthis claimed an attack on a Saudi Aramco refinery in Jizan. Maersk, rerouting around Africa, lifted full-year profit guidance to $6.5 billion.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic sits near the low end of its own range, and the pressure is coming from the west: Hormuz vessel transits have fallen to a fraction, squeezing the Gulf crude that Malaysian refineries take through this strait. Volumes ran within a few percent of the 90-day baseline through mid-August, with calm seas.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic is running about 12% above its 90-day baseline, with a swing from 28 vessels on Jul 10 to 401 on Jul 12 that tracks Typhoon Dolphin-scale disruption, when China cancelled flights and ordered evacuations. Military pressure is steady alongside it: China's coast guard now patrols east of Taiwan.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Traffic sits near 33 vessels a day, down slightly against its own 90-day baseline, with the series swinging from 83 on Jul 13 to 22 on Jul 22. The input does not explain those swings.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Transits fell to 37 vessels a day, down 28% on the 90-day baseline and well below the 100 counted on Jun 9, as attacks on Black Sea shipping mounted: a third Greek vessel burned in three days to Aug 18, TASS says Russia struck 130 ships since July, and Ukraine hit the Russian port of Novorossiysk.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic has barely moved: the last seven days sit 0.4% below the 90-day baseline, with 150 vessels a day at the latest reading. The swing across the window was narrow, from a low of 111 on Jun 3 to a high of 163 on Jun 13, and nothing on record accounts for either end.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic held near its own baseline through the window, with the 84-day span running between 186 vessels a day on Aug 1 and 126 on Aug 3 and no weather alert against it. Nothing in the period explains the swing; the last seven days sit 3.2 percent below the 90-day norm.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic sits near its 84-day average after a run-up to 123 vessels on Jul 31, with a low of 68 on Jul 4. Shipping through Hormuz has slowed to a near halt as a 60-day deadline for a US-Iran MoU expired, and a Russia-linked tanker explosion off Oman spread a slick toward the coast — the kind of risk that pushes owners onto the Cape route.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has fallen to zero, down about 95% against its own 90-day baseline, as the Black Sea shipping war widened: a third Greek vessel in three days burned there, and Ukrainian drones struck the Russian port of Novorossiysk. Russia is now rationing gasoline and importing fuel at lower standards.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index has drifted down about two percent over the past month, through a stretch in which Houthi drones hit the Aramco refinery at Jazan on 9 August — a plant processing 400,000 barrels of crude daily — and Saudi Arabia signed a mutual defence pact with Turkiye and Pakistan in Mecca.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index has climbed about a tenth over the quarter, through a period in which Ankara passed a law aimed at Kurdish disarmament and Turkey deepened its regional role — signing a mutual defence pact in Mecca with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, and routing 70 long-range US missiles to Ukraine. None of that coverage explains the June 18 high directly.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index sits well below its June high after Iran fired two ballistic missiles at the UAE on 18 August, triggering Dubai's first emergency alert in months, and Abu Dhabi responded by suspending all trade and financial transactions with Iran. Two ADNOC tankers had already been struck transiting Hormuz five days earlier.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index has drifted down from its Aug 5 high of 1748 after Hormuz vessel transits fell to a fraction of normal, cutting Gulf crude flows to Malaysian refineries. Over the full window it is still up, having climbed from 1657 on Jul 1.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index has climbed to a two-month high, and the policy backdrop settled during the run: Prabowo named a central bank deputy as the new governor, and the rupiah rose slightly on the news. Nothing in the market's path was interrupted by the Flores quake or the Bali ferry fire.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range after recovering from a Jul 29 low of 61,430. The window covered a run of shocks around Japan rather than in its market: North Korea's ballistic launch on Aug 12, Putin's visit to the disputed Kuril Islands that drew a Japanese protest, and torrential rains that killed 8 people.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index sits near the top of its 64-day range after recovering from a late-June low, with Chinese corporate news running heavily to industrial and technology strength: Alibaba banked more than $2 billion selling its Lingxi games unit, LandSpace landed a stainless-steel orbital booster, and a record 540,000 EVs left China last month. Against that, July retail sales rose just 0.6%.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index sits about 4% below its late-June level, and the domestic demand picture behind it stayed weak: retail sales rose just 0.6% in July, and Evergrande's sentencing closed a chapter on the property collapse still weighing on household balance sheets. Industrial exports ran the other way, with a record 540,000 EVs leaving China last month.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The index sits about a tenth below its June high after bottoming on Jul 30, and has been climbing since. Hanwha's wheeled howitzer beat four US rivals for an Army contract on Aug 19, extending Korea's arms export run; a $880 billion domestic AI build-out is under way. North Korea fired a ballistic missile on Aug 12 ahead of US-South Korea drills.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range after a high of 78,950 on Aug 6, with little movement on the day. A 70-member Indian delegation arrived in Singapore on Aug 19 for trade talks, and two domestic policy fights are live: an adviser challenged the E20 ethanol mandate, and India may end a decade of free digital payments as the zero-MDR subsidy expires.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index has climbed roughly a fifth over the window, reaching 5,768 on Aug 17 from a low of 4,959 on Jun 10. A 70-member Indian delegation arrived in Singapore on Aug 19 for the India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable, led by Sitharaman and Goyal, focused on tech, investment and trade ties.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index has recovered from its 39,930 low on Jul 30 without the pressure on Taipei easing: China's coast guard now patrols east of Taiwan, Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy there, and Taiwan said AI agents extracted passwords over four days in a hacking campaign. Traders have not priced the sovereignty question.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits at its 40-day high after a 6.9% climb from the May low, without a clear driver in view. Bangkok's news has run to diplomacy rather than markets: Thailand is courting cybersecurity cooperation with Russia, trade between the two is up 23% in January-May, and Bangkok hosted Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index climbed through a run of impeachment testimony against Sara Duterte in Manila, where a former disbursing officer said Duterte ordered a P125-million transfer to a security officer and auditors found confidential funds paid to unusual names. The market has treated the trial as contained, not as a threat to the wider institutional order.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index sits near a record after the RBA held rates steady on 11 August, with the housing market softening and another hike still on the table. It has climbed about 5% over the window, peaking at 9,272 on Aug 6 before easing ahead of inflation data due later in August.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index climbed to a series high of 117,700 on 21 August, up 3.2% over the window from its 23 July low of 108,300. Nothing in the record explains the move.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: Petrobras detected signs of oil off the Amazon coast, and Lula called the new Amazon oil a "passport" — a frontier prospect for a market whose largest listings are resource companies. Separately, Brasilia ordered Discord to suspend livestreams, and an investigation of a banking hack led to arrests in Germany and Brazil.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index sits near the low end of its range after Washington cancelled the US visa of Andrés Manuel López Beltrán, son of the former president, drawing a public rebuke from Claudia Sheinbaum. It touched 63,930 on Aug 18 before a 2.1% daily rebound.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The index sits well below its 22 July high of 3,380,000 after weeks of decline. The one story in the window is the 18 August arrest of a Milei adviser over the shooting of lawyer Nadia Beller in Santa Cruz de la Sierra, which does not explain the market move.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: Trade talks with Washington collapsed on Friday and 50% US tariffs took effect, with Ottawa promising a dollar-for-dollar response from September 8. Canada refused an offer to cut tariffs on steel, aluminium and autos and scrap the lumber tariff. The index still sits near its Aug 13 high of 36,760.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index reached 7799 on Aug 13 and has eased since, closing at 7674 on Aug 21, up 2.7 percent over the past three months. Defence contracting ran heavily through the period — the Pentagon awarded Raytheon a $22.9 billion Tomahawk contract — while trade friction persisted, with Canada rejecting US relief on heavy trucks. China's robotics component ban left US startups unable to buy the parts they need.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The index sits near the top of its 66-day range, having climbed from its Jun 9 low of 10230 to a Jul 29 high of 10910. Oil above $91 after Trump signaled he won't renew the Iran deal lifts the heavily weighted energy names, while regulators opened drip-pricing probes into Virgin Atlantic and Trainline.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index has climbed through a run of European security and energy news: Croatia's arrest of a second Nord Stream suspect on 19 August, Berlin doubling its anti-drone force after an explosive-laden drone was found at Leipzig/Halle Airport, and Kallas pressing the EU's broadest Russia sanctions package yet. It peaked at 26,440 on 14 August.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The index has climbed roughly 5% over the window, reaching 8,726 on Aug 10 before easing to 8,484. Nothing in the period's French news explains the move: the days around the peak were dominated by record heat and low water on the Seine, and jellyfish swarms that knocked out 3.2 gigawatts of nuclear power at Gravelines.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index has climbed nearly 7% over the window, reaching 1,120 on Aug 13 before easing to 1,106. Nothing in the Amsterdam news of the period explains the run: the local stories were a cyberattack that froze eight CEVA warehouses across Europe, root-level exploitation of Mac screen sharing, and low water on the Rhine at Nijmegen.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index rose 11.05% over the window to 19,960, peaking at 20,210 on Aug 11. Nothing in the material accounts for the move.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index has climbed roughly 7% over the window, reaching 53,720 on Aug 7 before easing to 52,670. The feed does not carry an Italian market story that explains the move.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The index has climbed steadily to 14,460, up about 7.5 percent across the window, with its high of 14,630 reached on Aug 10 and its low of 13,220 back on Jun 3. Nothing in the available material explains the rise.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index sits near the top of its range, up 5.7% over the window and 1% on the day, after a high of 3327 on Aug 5. The available material does not explain the move.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The index has given up roughly 9% across the past 64 days. It peaked at 4463 on May 25, fell to a low of 3966 on Jun 29, and has traded close to that floor since, ending at 4059 after a slight rise on the day. The available material does not explain the decline.

wiki-turkey.standing: The daily count of people reading the English Wikipedia article on Turkey, a rough measure of how many outsiders are looking the country up. It rises when Turkey is doing something that draws attention abroad rather than at home.
wiki-turkey.recent: The 25 July peak came as Turkey moved on two fronts at once: parliament passed a law on Kurdish disarmament that never names Abdullah Öcalan's release, and Ankara joined Saudi Arabia and Pakistan in a mutual defence pact whose defence chiefs and foreign ministers now form a standing bloc. Moscow then said the transfer of 70 long-range US missiles to Ukraine via Turkey undermines trust.

xag.standing: A dollar-per-ounce silver price, quoted through a token backed by physical metal. Silver is both a store of value and an industrial input — solar cells, electronics, brazing — so it answers to investor demand and factory demand at once.
xag.recent: The price sits at 51.56 an ounce, about 9% below where the 31-day window opened. The path there was extreme: a low of 29.8 on Aug 6 and a high of 67.31 on Aug 20, a range of more than double inside two weeks, with the fall from that peak taking three days.

wiki-osun-state.standing: One of Nigeria's 36 states, in the Yoruba southwest, with a governorship election on its own off-cycle calendar — which makes it one of the few contests the whole country can watch alone, and a rehearsal for how national votes will be run and disputed.
wiki-osun-state.recent: Readership tracked Osun's governorship vote on 15 August: voters queued calmly across the state, 146 suspected political thugs and a lawmaker were arrested, and the peak on 16 August came as Adeleke led the count by 67,232 votes and rivals conceded within a day. Civil society groups tallied 56 incidents and 14 deaths.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the US Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate untouched at a given meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves whenever the rate path is repriced — and mortgage, credit and currency costs follow the rate itself.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Fed minutes released on 19 August showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, and the contract on no change has climbed from 39 on Aug 1 to 69, after peaking at 75 on Aug 15. The venue itself has been under pressure through the same weeks: JPMorgan debanked Polymarket, and South Korea joined more than 30 jurisdictions restricting access.

poly-will-alexandria-ocasio-cortez-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez wins the 2028 US presidential election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on candidate news and on who else is seen entering the field, not on polling alone.
poly-will-alexandria-ocasio-cortez-win-t.recent: The move came against a month of scrutiny of Polymarket itself rather than of the candidate: a research group identified 152 wallets with a 97.2% win rate betting on US military operations, JPMorgan cut the venue off while still courting it, and a federal order forced a rival prediction market to keep operating in New York over a state ban.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out on whether the US-Iran ceasefire is still holding at a set date. It is a bet, not a forecast: the price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each strike, threat and lapsed talk.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: The odds firmed after a week in which the fighting stayed economic rather than kinetic: Washington swapped strikes for slow strangulation, the UAE cut off Iran trade and finance, and Rezaei's threats to Gulf neighbours came as words. The low on Aug 19 sat alongside reports Tehran had weighed strikes on Bulgaria and Cyprus.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency whose ledger hides sender, receiver and amount by default, unlike Bitcoin's public chain. That privacy makes it the settlement currency of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and a recurring target of exchange delistings.
xmr.recent: Monero climbed to $432.8 on Aug 23, its high for the month, after outperforming Bitcoin and ether earlier in August. The month's ransomware news ran alongside it: CISA identified more than 200 Medusa victims, the FBI and South Korea warned of Gunra targeting critical infrastructure, and a Ukrainian developer went on trial in Switzerland.

wiki-lebanon.standing: A count of how many people open Wikipedia's Lebanon article each day. It rises when the country enters the news, and the shape of the curve marks which days a story broke and how long it held.
wiki-lebanon.recent: The peak on Aug 21 came as families in Beirut prepared to demand an ICC trial over Israeli strikes that have killed 28 journalists since 2023. Earlier attention followed the Aug 15 strike near Ansar that destroyed a house and killed seven, and strikes on Aug 17 that killed 11.

wiki-petroleum.standing: The general article on crude oil and its refined products — the substance itself, not a price. Readership tracks the moments when fuel becomes political: a supply route closes, a subsidy changes, a new field is found.
wiki-petroleum.recent: Views peaked on Aug 13 and have fallen since, as the news moved from crude itself to the countries handling it: Kazakhstan's oil export share fell from 52.9% to 46.5% in a year, Pakistan raised diesel Rs6.47 to Rs390.42 a litre, and a crude line burst under homes in Karachi. Lula called new Amazon oil a "passport.

stocks:BCS.standing: A British bank listed in London and New York, with a large investment-banking arm alongside its UK high-street business. Its share price tracks UK credit conditions, interest rates and trading revenue, and it is a frequent target of political campaigns.
stocks:BCS.recent: Barclays shares drifted lower across the window, from 28.56 on Jul 27 to 26.83, with the low of 26.05 two days after the high. The one story attached to the bank in this period is a Preston court ruling that £212,805 of damage caused by five Palestine activists at a Barclays branch was not serious enough for terrorism sentencing.
